dossier.overview:
An `.owmap` file is the binary overworld map format (v1, magic `OWM1`) shared between the **Operations Desk Map Editor** and the Pokémon Resort C++ loader. On disk it still combines a fast binary header, a UTF-8 metadata JSON blob, and three packed terrain layers (height, special ramps, collision bits).

What changed in practice: the **metadata JSON** now carries the live map state the game renders: **RTPKS tile paint layers** (`tileLayers` with `resortTileId` per cell), a bound **tile package** (`tilePackage`), optional **path paint** (`pathLayer`), placed **GLB props** (`models[]`), NPC slots, spawn, and camera. The Map Editor paints tiles from **RTPKS v2** packs (see rtpks-format); the runtime loads the same pack through `RtpksTilePackageLoader` and draws tiles in **bgfx** (`OverworldBgfxRenderer`).

Maps save to `pokemon-resort/assets/overworld/maps/*.owmap`. Canonical encode/decode: `pokemon-resort-page/tools/admin/lib/owmap-format.mjs`. Short spec: `pokemon-resort/docs/gameplay/owmap_format.md`.

blocks.body:
Runtime default for the 3D test screen: `assets/overworld/maps/testing.owmap` (`Overworld3DTestScreen.cpp`).

**On disk:** binary header + `metaJson` (includes `tileLayers`, `tilePackage`, `models[]`, spawn, camera) + packed `height` / `special` / `collision` grids.

**In the editor:** full grids and tile layer cells live in memory. **Save .owmap** runs `bakeTerrainSpecials()` then `encodeOwmap()` (terrain stripped from JSON, appended as binary).

**At runtime:** `parseSceneMetadata()` reads `tilePackage` and `tileLayers`; `OverworldBgfxRenderer` instantiates RTPKS meshes per cell and depth-sorts with props and characters.

sections.title: Schema reference
sections.summary: Binary container, terrain grids, RTPKS decoration layers (up to 7), and JSON metadata.

blocks.body: Little-endian, version 1. Row-major indexing for all terrain layers: `index = y * width + x`. The JSON metadata block never contains terrain grids: `encodeOwmap()` calls `stripTerrainForMeta()` before stringify.

blocks.html:
OffsetSizeField
04magic OWM1 (0x4F574D31)
42version u16 = 1
62width u16 (1…256)
82height u16 (1…256)
104tileSize f32 (typically 16)
144metaLen u32
18NmetaJson UTF-8 (N = metaLen)
18+NW×Hheight[] u8 per cell
…W×Hspecial[] u8 per cell
…⌈W×H/8⌉collision bits (1 = blocked)

Collision packing: cell (x,y) → bit index i = y*W + x → byte i >> 3, bit i & 7. Unpacked at runtime to u8 0/1 grids.

blocks.title: File structure
blocks.caption: Reader validates exact payload size: no trailing bytes
blocks.source:
flowchart TD
    H[18-byte header] --> J[metaJson UTF-8]
    J --> HT[height W×H bytes]
    HT --> SP[special W×H bytes]
    SP --> CO[collision ceil W×H/8 bytes]
    CO --> SC[SceneConfig via parseSceneMetadata + grids]

blocks.caption: encodeOwmap: pack header, JSON, and terrain layers
loadOwmapScene: validate magic, dimensions, parse JSON, unpack grids

blocks.body: These three **binary** layers are packed after `metaJson` in every `.owmap`. They define walkable geometry (height, ramps, blocked cells). **RTPKS decoration** is separate: up to seven `tileLayers` in metadata (next tab).

blocks.html:
LayerStorageRangeMeaning
heightu8 per cell0…255Discrete height level; multiplied by tileSize for world Y
specialu8 per cell0…13Ramp / corner shape (see table below)
collision1 bit per cell0/11 = blocked for pathfinding and player movement

specialLabelOn disk?
0Flatyes
1Auto ramp (editor)no: baked to 2–5 or cleared on save
2Ramp northyes
3Ramp eastyes
4Ramp southyes
5Ramp westyes
6–9Convex corners NE/SE/SW/NWyes
10–13Concave corners NE/SE/SW/NWyes

Auto ramp (1) infers cardinal direction from neighbor height deltas in the editor preview. On save, bakeTerrainSpecials() writes 2–5 or clears to 0. The game loader logs an error if special==1 is still present: always re-export from the Map Editor before shipping.

blocks.body: **Special tile** brush: ramp cardinals (stored on the lower-height cell), convex/concave corners, and editor-only auto ramps (baked on save). Glyphs overlay the height tint. Ownership matches runtime: a north ramp on `(x,y)` means the north neighbor is one height level taller.
blocks.caption: Special tile / ramp editor

blocks.body: **Collider** view paints impassable bits (red overlay). Separate from height and RTPKS decoration layers. Pathfinding and player movement respect blocked cells; ramp specials still govern step-up separately.
blocks.caption: 2D collider view
bakeTerrainSpecials: resolve AUTO (1) before encodeOwmap

blocks.body: **`tileLayers`** stores RTPKS mesh placement: the same stacking idea as PDSMS map layers 0–7, but each cell holds a stable **`resortTileId`** (from the bound `.rtpks` pack), not a PDSMS local index. Maps support **up to 7 decoration layers** (`MAX_TILE_LAYERS` in the Map Editor). Layer 0 is drawn first (ground); higher indices stack on top. Empty cells are `null` in JSON and **-1** in C++ (`TileLayerConfig::cells`).

Layer chips on the left switch the active decoration layer. The 2D view composites visible layers bottom-to-top; the topmost non-empty tile at a cell is what you see in the thumbnail. Multi-cell RTPKS tiles anchor at the painted cell and occupy footprint cells on that layer only.
blocks.caption: Seven decoration layers: tile paint view

blocks.html:
FieldTypeNotes
tileLayers.versionnumberEditor schema version (currently 1)
tileLayers.activeLayernumberWhich layer the Map Editor paints on (0-based)
tileLayers.layers[]array1…7 entries; excess trimmed on load
layers[].idstringStable id e.g. ground, path, detail_a
layers[].namestringDisplay label in editor UI
layers[].visiblebooleanHidden layers skip 2D composite and runtime draw
layers[].cells[y][x]number | nullresortTileId from bound RTPKS; empty = no tile

blocks.title: Per-cell stack
blocks.caption: Each (x,y) can hold one tile per decoration layer; runtime iterates layers in order
blocks.source:
flowchart BT
    L0[Layer 0 ground] --> L1[Layer 1 paths]
    L1 --> L2[Layer 2 detail …]
    L2 --> L6[Layer 6 top overlay]
    L6 --> DRAW[OverworldBgfxRenderer depth sort]

blocks.html:
Default layer names (Map Editor seeds these when creating a map): Ground, Paths, Detail A, Detail B, Overlay: you can add more up to the 7-layer cap.

Runtime placement (OverworldBgfxRenderer): for each visible layer in order, non-empty cells load runtime/meshes/tile_{resortTileId}.json from the bound pack. Each layer index adds a small Y lift (layer_index × 0.004 world units) so stacked tiles do not z-fight. Tiles sit on terrain height from the binary height grid at their anchor cell.

Requires tilePackage pointing at an RTPKS v2 file on disk. Without a bound pack, decoration layers are stored but not rendered.

blocks.caption: applyTileLayersConfig: parse layers[] into SceneConfig

blocks.body:
Metadata is everything except packed `terrain` grids. Parsed by `SceneMetadataParser.cpp` into `SceneConfig`. Paths are relative to the game project root unless absolute.

The parser merges `config/gameplay/world3d/defaults.json`, camera presets, `sprites/shadow.json`, and `world3d/render.json` before applying map fields. **Tile paint** (`tileLayers`) and **tile package** (`tilePackage`) are read from map JSON and drive RTPKS mesh placement at runtime. Door travel uses `anchors[]`, `links[]`, and `doorTriggers[]`. A visible door trigger points to an RTPKS tile; an invisible door omits that visual reference.

blocks.body:
What does **not** belong in metadata:

• Party / box Pokémon state (use Resort + OpenHome; see compatibility-ontology)
• Per-session follower config (see follower-pokemon / session.json)
• Map-level wild Pokémon spawn tables: not in v1 yet (see overworld_pokemon_architecture_handoff.md in the game repo)

blocks.body:
Workflow:

1. In **PDSMS**, save tiles as **RTPKS v2** (`.rtpks` + `.rtpks.meta` sidecar). Copy both to `pokemon-resort/assets/overworld/tilepacks/`.
2. `npm run admin` → **Map Editor** → set maps folder and **tile packages** folder → **Refresh**.
3. Load or create a map → **Bind tile package** → paint `tileLayers`, terrain, collision, and props.
4. Open **Doors**. Add a move-toward trigger, select its approach direction and script, and connect it to a destination map anchor. A trigger coordinate may sit one cell outside the map for a walk-through doorway.
5. For a visible door, attach an RTPKS tile reference. The visual can point to this map or another map, which lets an interior return script close the exterior tile after teleport. Leave it empty for an invisible trigger.
6. **Save .owmap** (bakes auto ramps, writes binary + metadata JSON).
7. Run the game 3D test screen to verify RTPKS placement, door animation, circular transition, teleport, and the authored exit step.

Legacy `.map.json` imports still round-trip through `mapFromJson()` before save.

sections.title: Writer vs reader
sections.summary: Same OWM1 v1 layout in JavaScript and C++.

blocks.caption: Paths relative to each repo root.

blocks.body: The Map Editor holds a JSON-shaped map object. Save triggers `bakeTerrainSpecials()` then `encodeOwmap()` in `server.mjs` → `writeMapOwmap()`. Terrain never appears inside `metaJson` on disk.

blocks.caption: decodeOwmap: re-open saved maps in the editor

blocks.body:
`loadOwmapScene()` unpacks terrain grids, then `parseSceneMetadata()` fills `SceneConfig` including `tile_package` and `tile_layers`. `RtpksTilePackageLoader` opens the bound **RTPKS v2** file; `OverworldBgfxRenderer` places each non-empty `tileLayers` cell using the mesh + materials from `runtime/meshes/tile_{id}.json`.

Billboard characters and GLB props depth-sort with RTPKS tiles using ground-anchor bias from `render.json`.

blocks.caption: parseSceneMetadata: defaults merge, render/shadow, models

sections.title: How to extend the format
sections.summary: Version bumps, new metadata, and loader coordination.

blocks.body:
**Safe extensions (v1):**

• Add optional keys to metadata JSON: update `SceneMetadataParser.cpp` to read them; old maps ignore unknown fields
• Add new `special` tile IDs (14+): coordinate with `ramp-specials.js`, Map Editor presets, and `OverworldMapRenderer.cpp` corner math
• Add NPC `movementProfile` values: extend `parseMovementProfile()` and editor dropdown

**Breaking changes:**

• Bump `version` u16 in the binary header (currently 1) and teach both `decodeOwmap()` and `OwmapOverworldLoader.cpp` to accept the new version
• Change grid packing (e.g. wider collision flags): requires coordinated writer/reader change
• Never store terrain inside `metaJson`: keeps editor round-trip and binary size predictable

Update `pokemon-resort/docs/gameplay/owmap_format.md` and this article in the same change.

blocks.title: Extension decision flow
blocks.caption: Prefer optional JSON fields before bumping binary version
blocks.source:
flowchart TD
    Q[Need new map data?] --> A{Terrain per cell?}
    A -->|Yes| B{Fits special layer?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Add special ID + renderer]
    B -->|No| D[Consider v2 grid or metadata tile map]
    A -->|No| E[Optional metadata JSON key]
    E --> F[SceneMetadataParser + editor UI]
